missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend potassium based only on sweat level; assess duration, conditions, diet, hydration, product composition, kidney status and medicines.
safety_exclusions: Do not infer potassium deficiency from sweating or cramps alone.
Do not recommend potassium tablets or salt substitutes without medical and medication review.
Do not conflate sodium and potassium replacement needs.
professional_escalation_conditions: Kidney disease, heart failure, known hyperkalemia, ACE inhibitor/ARB or potassium-sparing diuretic use, palpitations or weakness.
population_and_context: People reporting high sweat loss during exercise; sweat-related fluid and electrolyte losses do not by themselves establish a need for isolated potassium supplementation.
dose_constraints: No potassium dose from this rule. Exercise hydration/electrolyte strategy must be based on event duration, sweat rate, diet and appropriate sports guidance.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Potassium and Exercise fact sheets provide general potassium and exercise context; high sweat loss alone does not justify isolated potassium supplementation.
